title: The Forest Edge
caption: The wood everyone says grew by itself.

year.means: the years since the prologue, as the place has them: 0 — the bare slope, the stream dry, the village dying (the prologue and the first chapter); 6 — the young oaks above the head, the water back (the second chapter); 20 — the grown forest (the third chapter, fourteen years on); 30 — the epilogue, ten years more

stream.means: the stream running in its bed (the water, the rushes, the green banks); false — the dry bed, white with stones (the first chapter)

mist.means: morning mist low over the slope: 0 none, 1 thick (the first chapter's morning)

morning.means: the light's look: 0 the summer afternoon, 1 an early morning, cooler and hazier (the first chapter's planting). The sky is painted as morning above a half: set it at once

bread.means: a loaf in a linen cloth lies on the flat stone by the path where it enters the wood (left for Elzéard, untouched); false — the stone bare

smoke.means: the smoke from the village's chimneys far below: 0 none, 1 three hearths lit

sheep.means: Elzéard's sheep grazing the bare meadow right of the path (the first chapter)

dog.means: the shepherd's dog lying in the meadow minding the sheep (the first chapter)

hives.means: at the edge's foot across the stream: hives — Elzéard's five hives (2.5; 3.1 when Lina does not know); stands — only the flat stones they stood on, the hives taken to his house (3.1 when Lina knows); none

stumps.means: the felling of the forest's near (lower) edge, over the path to the village: none; begun — the two oaks by the hives cut, fresh stumps (3.1, Lina does not know); lower — the whole lower edge felled, fresh stumps (3.5 on Silence); begun_old — those two, ten years on, old stumps grown about with undergrowth (the epilogue on the Name, Lina did not know); lower_old — the lower edge ten years on: old stumps and young oaks a man's height between them (the epilogue on Silence)

stump_bread.means: a loaf in a cloth laid on a stump of the felled lower edge (3.5 on Silence, when Lina knows)

own_oak.means: the Traveller's own oak by the stone, a little crooked (he planted it himself in 1.4: «Свой дуб»)

beeches.means: the Traveller's beeches: slope — he stayed, his beeches on the meadow across the stream from the forest (young in the third chapter, above the head in the epilogue); row — he went on the Road, one beech a year in a row by the path (how many: beech_row); none

beech_row.means: how many beeches stand in the Road's row (with beeches "row"): 13 as he comes in the third chapter, 14 once he plants the year's, 24 in the epilogue; each as tall as its years. The next one's place is beech_next

board.means: the board at the forest's edge: «Elzéard's Forest. Protected. No fires.» (the epilogue on the Name)

rod_ground.means: an iron rod stuck upright in the ground, at rod_a/rod_d (1.4: Elzéard left it in the earth; the final «Two Rods»: his rod beside the Traveller's)

rod_a.means: where the rod in the ground stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

rod_d.means: where the rod in the ground stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

pail.means: a pail set down on the ground at pail_a/pail_d: acorns — soaking for the day's planting (the first chapter); leaves — seeds wrapped in leaves torn from the Traveller's notebook (the final «Two Rods»); none

pail_a.means: where the pail stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

pail_d.means: where the pail stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

beech_next_a.means: where the next beech of the Road's row goes (the script's, from beech_row): metres right

beech_next_d.means: where the next beech of the Road's row goes (the script's, from beech_row): metres ahead

moment.means: which moment of the scenario the forest's edge shows (script.js lays it out; notes.md): planting — 1.1–1.4, the bare slope, the first chapter's morning; grove — 2.5, the young oaks above the head, six years on; edge — 3.1, the grown forest fourteen years on; delegation — 3.2–3.3, the town's people come; stumps — 3.5 on Silence, the lower edge felled; board — the final «The Board» (the epilogue); pupil — the final «The Pupil»; two_rods — the final «Two Rods»

staged.means: the moment the script last laid out (the script's own: it lays a moment out again only when this differs)

elzeard_a.means: where Elzéard stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

elzeard_d.means: where Elzéard stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

traveller_a.means: where the Traveller stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

traveller_d.means: where the Traveller stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

lina_a.means: where Lina stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

lina_d.means: where Lina stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

jan_a.means: where Jan stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

jan_d.means: where Jan stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

chief_a.means: where the chief from town stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

chief_d.means: where the chief from town stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

ranger_a.means: where the ranger stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

ranger_d.means: where the ranger stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

axeman_a.means: where the man with the axe stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

axeman_d.means: where the man with the axe stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

visitor_a_a.means: where the visitor with the basket stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

visitor_a_d.means: where the visitor with the basket stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

visitor_b_a.means: where the visitor with the notebook stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

visitor_b_d.means: where the visitor with the notebook stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

boy_a.means: where the boy stands, metres right of the view's line (the moment sets it)

boy_d.means: where the boy stands, metres ahead (the moment sets it)

new_beech.means: the beech sapling the Traveller plants this year (МИ4) at new_beech_a/d: none; crooked — it stands askew; straight

new_beech_a.means: where this year's beech is planted, metres right (the piece `beech` sets it: the row's next place or his slope)

new_beech_d.means: where this year's beech is planted, metres ahead

silent.means: the game's: at Ш2 the Traveller said nothing (Jan grips his shoulder in the piece `unnamed`); false — he said «it grew by itself»

beat_next.means: the piece the game plays next (modules/beats: made ready ahead)

prompts.text: Solo nylon-string guitar, slow sparse fingerpicking, long silences between phrases, warm and wistful
Soft wooden flute over a low drone, open fifths, a lonely high plateau at dusk
Quiet felt piano, few notes, lots of air, like wind over dry grass
Ambient pads of distant wind, barely moving, golden evening light
Pastoral folk waltz on accordion and violin, gentle and old-fashioned
Cello and harp duet, slow and tender, a sense of patience
Minimalist marimba patterns, slowly growing, like seedlings
Shepherd's pipe melody, modal, unaccompanied, echoing across hills
String quartet, sustained hopeful chords, slow build
Music box lullaby, simple and fragile, slightly out of tune
Warm clarinet over soft strings, nostalgic, unhurried
Hammered dulcimer, gentle repeating figure, morning mist
Low bowed double bass and wind, sparse and dry, a dead land
Choir humming softly in the distance, no words, reverent
Mandolin tremolo, quiet and bittersweet, a village at evening
Glassy electric piano with tape warmth, calm and spacious
Solo violin, plain slow melody, the bow almost whispering
Birdsong-like woodwinds over a gentle string bed, a forest waking
Running water and a soft celesta, a stream heard for the first time, quiet wonder
